First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 7
Chapter 6.2: Voter Registration 
Prior to Election Day
Sec. 6.2.1: Voter Registration Basics
Figure 1: Voter registration timeline
Note: while registration is not permissible during the Saturday and 
Sunday before Election Day, in-person absentee voting is allowed.
“ERO” means an “Election Registration Official”
All voters must be registered before being issued a ballot unless specifically 
exempt from registration. Wis. Stat. § 6.27. New and former Wisconsin residents 
voting Presidential-only ballots are not required to register, and military electors 
voting by absentee ballot are also not required to register. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.15, 6.18, 
6.22(3). Note: Although military voters are not required to register, they may still 
choose to do so. Military voters can utilize special federal forms to accomplish 
registration. For more information about how military voters may register to 
vote, see Sec. 7.4.9: “Methods for Voter Registration for UOCAVA Voters.”
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 8
Sec. 6.2.2: Methods of Registration
Note:  There are only four acceptable methods 1 to register to vote. 
Voters cannot scan and email or fax voter registration applications. 
Wis. Stat. § 6.30(4) .
Method 1: By Mail
Application
The voter must complete and sign a Voter Registration Application (EL-131), 
enclose a copy of their proof of residence, and mail the completed application 
to the municipal clerk’s office. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.30(4), 6.34(2).
The Commission has determined that voter registrations made “by mail” also 
include registrations that are submitted to the municipal clerk by people or 
groups on behalf of voters. Statute does not further define “by mail” in the 
context of the voter registration statute, but a provision of the Commission’s 
administrative code defines it to mean “the completing and signing of a 
voter registration application form other than in the presence of a special 
registration deputy, county clerk, deputy clerk, or municipal clerk.”  
Wis. Admin. Code § EL 3.01(4). Accordingly, registrations need not solely be 
returned by USPS, FedEx, or UPS to be considered submitted “by mail” under 
Wis. Stat. § 6.30(4).
Incomplete Applications
Registrants who submit incomplete voter registration applications or fail to 
provide a copy of proof of residence when required shall be contacted within 
five days, if possible, by their municipal clerk. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2). The registrant 
should be instructed that the registration is incomplete and notified about how 
to repair the deficiency. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2). Statute directs that the clerk request 
that the voter appear at the clerk’s office or another registration location to 
complete the registration. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2).
1 Excluding military voters.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 9
Best Practice: The Missing POR Notification Letter (EL-132)  
is a customizable template letter that a clerk should send 
to anyone who has not submitted proof of residence 
with their voter registration when required.
Any insufficiency must be rectified no later than the 20th day before the election,  
by mail, or delivered in-person no later than 5:00 p.m. the Friday before the 
election. They can also register again on Election Day at the polls despite the 
prior insufficient registration attempt. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(3).
Administrative Follow-Up
The clerk or deputy should review the application and the enclosed proof of 
residence to ensure the application is legible and complete before signing 
and dating the application. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(1). The clerk shall then enter the 
registration information into WisVote. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(4).
The Commission will mail a voter verification postcard to the voter’s residential 
address as listed on the Voter Registration Application. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(4).
Timing
The application must be postmarked no later than the 20th day (which is the 
third Wednesday) before the election. Wis. Stat. § 6.28(1)(a).
A registrant who postmarks their application after the 20th day before the 
election should be advised, preferably in writing, that their application cannot 
be processed until after Election Day. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(3). Clerks are required 
to make a “good faith effort” to contact voters who submit by-mail voter 
registration applications after the close of registration. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(3). The 
registrant should also be advised of any remaining opportunities to register to 
vote in the coming election. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(3).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 10
Method 2: Online
Note: The deadline for online registration is 11:59 p.m. on the 3rd 
Wednesday preceding the election. Wis. Stat. § 6.28(1).
An eligible elector who holds a current, valid Wisconsin driver’s license or ID card 
can register to vote online at MyVote.wi.gov. Wis. Stat. § 6.30(5). When registering 
online, a voter gives the Commission authorization to obtain an electronic copy 
of their signature from the Wisconsin Department of Transportation for use 
in signing the application. Wis. Stat. § 6.30(5). The Commission then notifies 
individual clerks of new online registrations. Wis. Stat. § 6.30(5). Voters can also 
update their registration online. Wis. Stat. § 6.30(5).
Voters who register online are not required to provide proof of residence if 
they provide their driver’s license number, ID number, name, and date of birth, 
and the Commission is able to verify their information. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(2m), 
6.34(4). The Commission performs this verification instantly during the online 
registration process. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(4). If the instant match cannot be verified, 
the voter is directed to the Department of Transportation’s website so they can 
first update their information with DOT. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(4). Once they do, they 
can register online.
Method 3: In Person with the Municipal Clerk
Registration in person with the municipal clerk is available to voters until the 
third Friday before the election. Wis. Stat. § 6.29(2)(a), 6.30(1).
Best Practice: This type of registration, also known as “late 
registration,” can also be completed during in-person absentee 
voting, either at the clerk’s office or an alternate absentee 
ballot site. While the late registration statute does not refer to 
in-person absentee voting, the Commission believes that the 
intent of the late registration statute is to ensure that election 
officials can confirm that voters are registered before they vote, 
and that the failure to refer to the in person absentee voting was 
Legislative oversight and would lead to an unreasonable result.
The voter must sign a completed Voter Registration Application (EL-131) in the 
presence of the clerk or deputy. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 11
The voter must present the clerk or deputy with proof of residence.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2). The clerk or deputy must record the type, issuing entity, and  
the last few digits of the unique number associated with the proof of residence,  
if any. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)12. If such number is seven or more digits in length, 
the last four digits must be recorded. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)12. If the unique 
number is six or fewer digits in length, only the last two digits are required.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)12.
The clerk or deputy should first review the application to ensure the application 
is legible and complete and then sign and date the completed application.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
For all registrations in the clerk’s office after the 20th day before the election, 
the clerk or deputy must issue a Certificate of Registration (EL-133) to the voter, 
which they should present at the polling place before being issued a ballot.  
Wis. Stat. §§ 6.55(2)(c)2., 6.29(2)(b).
Note: The EL-133 must be issued even if the voter is also voting in-
person absentee at the same time.
Late Registration In-Person
For all registrations in the clerk’s office after the 20th day before the election, the 
clerk or deputy must review the Ineligible Voter List to confirm that the voter will 
not be ineligible to vote on the day of the election. Wis. Stat. § 6.29(2)(am).
 Ɋ If the name of the voter appears on the list, the clerk shall inform the 
voter that they are ineligible to register to vote per the Department of 
Corrections. Wis. Stat. § 6.29(2)(am).
 Ɋ If the voter agrees that they are ineligible, the registration should be 
rejected. Wis. Stat. § 6.29(2)(am).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 12
Best Practice: If the voter maintains that they are eligible to 
vote in the election, the clerk should make a reasonable effort 
to contact the Commission to verify their felony status.
 Ɋ If the Commission confirms the voter is eligible to vote, the  
clerk should document on the Voter Registration Application  
(EL-131) that they confirmed the voter’s status with the Commission 
and then allow them to proceed to register to vote.
 Ɋ If the Commission confirms that the voter is NOT eligible to vote 
or if the clerk is unable to contact the Commission, and the 
voter still maintains that they are eligible, the clerk should:
 Ɋ Give the voter the Ineligible Voter Information Sheet 
(EL-119) that explains what they need to do to resolve 
the issue with the Department of Corrections.
 Ɋ AND
 Ɋ Permit the voter to register to vote, but mark the 
Voter Registration Application (EL-131) and Certificate 
of Registration (EL-133) as “ineligible to vote per 
Department of Corrections.” Wis. Stat. § 6.29(2)(am).
Note: The late-registration application must be received no later than 
close of business or 5:00 p.m., whichever is later, on the Friday before 
the election. Wis. Stat. § 6.29(2)(a).
Method 4: At the Polling Place on Election 
Day (Election Day Registration)
For information on the EDR process, see Chapter 14.6: “Election Day 
Registration.” See Wis. Stat. § 6.55.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 13
Sec. 6.2.3: Completing the Voter 
Registration Application
Proper completion of the Voter Registration Application (EL-131) will ease the 
process of entering information into WisVote and ensure the voter will appear 
on the poll list for Election Day. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(2)(a). It is the municipal clerk’s 
responsibility to notify voters of any insufficiency in their registration application 
within 5 days, if possible. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2).
Best Practice: If the voter is missing proof of residence, the 
Missing POR Notification Letter (EL-132) is a customizable 
template that is available for this purpose.
Note: Any version of the EL-131 should be accepted by mail or in person 
as long as it contains proper voter information. Voter registration forms 
cannot be scanned and emailed or faxed.
Front Side of Voter Registration Application
This is a summary of each entry on the EL-131 voting registration form:
1. Qualifications
Registrants must be able to check each of the four boxes in this section. These 
boxes correlate with the legal qualifications for voting. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.02, 6.03.
The registrant can register at 17 years old if they will be 18 years old by the time 
of the next election. Wis. Stat. § 6.05. Note: a person less than 18 years of age 
cannot vote in a primary election even if they will be 18 years old on the date of 
the general election.
2. Your Name
The registrant should provide their full name as it appears both on their 
Wisconsin Driver License or Wisconsin DOT-issued Identification Card, if 
applicable, and the proof of residence document provided for box 8 on the 
form. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 14
3. About You
Date of Birth
Month, day, and year of birth is required. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
Best Practice: Voters should be encouraged to use all four digits 
of their year of birth (e.g. “1989” instead of “89”), but if someone 
writes the last two digits, the application should not be rejected.
Contact Information – Phone Number and Email Address (OPTIONAL)
Registration applications should not be rejected because a voter has failed to, or 
refuses to, provide their phone number or email address. Voters are not required 
to provide their phone number or email address, but doing so is useful in case 
the clerk needs to contact the voter to correct errors in the registration form or 
paperwork. Wis. Stat. § 6.32. Clerks can still contact voters at the addresses they 
provide, but email or phone may be quicker and more efficient to resolve issues 
in a timely manner.
Note: Be advised, any phone or email address provided becomes a 
public record.
4. The Address Where You Live
This is the voter’s address where they reside, which may be different than their 
mailing address. Wis. Stat. § 6.10.
This section will also be used to indicate military or permanent overseas 
statuses. Military voters are not required to register to vote but some choose 
to do so anyways. Wis. Stat. § 6.22(3). Overseas voters, both permanent 
and temporary, are required to register. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.24(3), 6.27. For more 
information on military and overseas voter registration, see Chapter 7.4: “Types 
of Absentee Voters: UOCAVA.”
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 15
5. Your Mailing Address (OPTIONAL)
Voters are not required to provide mailing addresses to register, though doing 
so is often a good idea in case their municipal clerk needs to contact them. 
Registration applications should not be rejected because a voter has failed to, 
or refused to, provide a mailing address.
Best Practice: If the registrant does not receive mail at 
their residential address, a mailing address should be 
provided. Failure to provide a valid mailing address may 
result in the voter registration being inactivated since they 
would not be able to receive the verification postcard.
6. Prior Registration Information
Name Change
A voter is required to re-register if they change their legal name.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.33(5)(a)1.
Best Practice: As it may take some time for a voter to receive 
proper documentation of their new legal name, a registered 
voter may continue to vote using their former name until the 
necessary documentation to re-register is received.
Address Change
A registered voter is required to re-register if they wish to vote from their new 
residence. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.10(1), 6.33(5)(a)1.
7. Identification
To complete the Voter Registration Application (EL-131) or online voter registration,  
the registrant must provide either a Wisconsin Driver License number or 
Wisconsin DOT-issued Identification Card number, or the last four digits of 
their Social Security Number. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1). This does NOT require visual 
confirmation by the clerk or an election inspector, and the voter may write down 
or recite the number if they choose. A voter cannot be required to show their  
WI Driver License, WI DOT-issued ID card, or Social Security card as a condition 
of registration, unless the voter is offering it as acceptable proof of residence. 
Wis. Stat. §§ 6.33(1), 6.34(2), (2m).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 16
Wisconsin Driver License or Wisconsin DOT-issued ID Card Number
If the registrant has been issued either a WI Driver License or WI DOT-issued 
ID Card that is unexpired or not canceled, they must provide the number 
and expiration date, even if the registrant’s driving privileges were revoked or 
suspended. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1) (requiring a “valid” license or ID).
Best Practice: If the registrant has a WI Driver License or  
WI DOT-Issued ID Card that is unexpired but does not have 
the number or expiration date readily available, they may call 
DMV at (608) 266-1069, option 1 to look up the information.
If the registrant has either a WI Driver License or WI DOT-Issued ID Card that is 
currently expired or canceled, they must provide the last 4 digits of the Social 
Security Number instead. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
Social Security Number – Last Four Digits
If the registrant has not been issued a WI Driver License or WI DOT-Issued ID 
Card or the document is expired or canceled, the registrant must provide the 
last 4 digits of their Social Security Number. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
If the registrant does not have either a WI Driver License or WI DOT-Issued ID 
Card and has not been issued a Social Security Number, they may indicate 
this by checking the box signifying they have none of these documents.  
Wis. Admin. Code § EL 3.04(3) (implementing 52 U.S.C. § 21083(5)(A)(ii)). Voters 
in this circumstance check the appropriate box on the EL-131 but still must be 
permitted to register to vote.
8. Proof of Residence
The registrant will affirm that they are providing a valid form of proof of 
residence with this application. The document must list the voter’s complete 
name and Wisconsin residential address. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(b).
9. Signature and Certification
The registrant should read this language before certifying that they are  
an eligible elector and have resided in the ward for at least 28 days.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.33(2)(b). They will provide their signature and the date they are 
signing. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(2)(b).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 17
10. Assistant
If the registrant required another person to complete this form on their 
behalf due to a physical disability, the assistant should sign and provide their 
residential address here. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(2)(a).
Official Use Only Section
The election official receiving the application (clerk, election inspector, election 
registration official)2 should review the proof of residence. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.32(2), 
6.33(1), 6.34.
Proof of Residence Types
At the top of the section, the official will circle the Proof of Residence type.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.33(2)(a).
The following are the Proof of Residence types listed by their abbreviations in 
the Voter Registration Application (EL-131). For more specific information on what 
constitutes sufficient proof of residence or is required in each category, See Sec. 
6.2.4 on page 21.
 Ɋ WI DL  – Wisconsin-Issued Driver License.
 Ɋ WI ID  – Wisconsin DOT-Issued Identification Card.
 Ɋ UTIL  – Any form of utility bill.
 Ɋ BANK/CC  – A bank or credit card statement.
 Ɋ PYCK  – Paycheck or Paystub.
 Ɋ STDNT ID  – A student ID that includes a photo (address not required).
 Ɋ GOV DOC  – Any government-issued document.
 Ɋ LSE  – A residential lease (may not be used to register by mail).
 Ɋ GOV ID  – Any other identification card or license issued by a Wisconsin 
governmental body or unit.
 Ɋ EMPL ID  – An identification card issued by an employer in the normal 
course of business and bearing a photo of the card holder.
2 Any staff member, or any other individual, appointed as an ERO would need to complete election offi -
cial training before registering any qualified elector to vote.” Wis. Stat. § 7.315(4).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 18
 Ɋ RES CARE  – A contract or intake document from an occupant of a 
residential care facilities that specifies the occupant currently resides in 
the facility.
 Ɋ TAX  – A real estate tax bill or receipt for the current year or the year 
preceding the date of the election.
 Ɋ HMLSS  – A signed letter on public or private social security agency 
letterhead identifying a homeless voter and describing the individual’s 
residence for voting purposes.
Proof of Residence Issuing Entity
The clerk should write the name of the entity that issued the proof of residence 
document. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1). This is necessary to ensure that the proof of 
residence satisfies one of the legal types. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a).
Examples: WI DMV, MG & E, WE Energies, etc.
Proof of Residence Number, if any
If a unique number associated with the proof of residence is seven or more digits  
in length, the last four digits should be recorded here. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)12. For 
example, bank accounts are usually ten digits long, but only the last four digits 
should be recorded.
If a unique number associated with the proof of residence is six or fewer digits 
in length, only the last two digits are recorded here. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)12. For 
example, if an ID has five digits, only the last two would be recorded.
Date Complete/POR Received
If the application is received via mail, the clerk should check the box indicating 
as such and enter the date in which it was received. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
Best Practice: If the application is complete and the 
proof of residence is acceptable (see below), the election 
official who received the application (election registration 
official, clerk or election inspector) should date it.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 19
Election Day Voter Number
If registering on Election Day, the voter will be issued a voter number before 
they are given their ballot. Wis. Stat. § 6.79(2)(b). This number should also 
be recorded on the supplemental poll list. Wis. Stat. § 6.79(2)(c). For more 
information on the Election Day Registration (EDR) procedures, see Chapter 14.6: 
“Election Day Registration.”
WisVote ID #
This number is assigned by the clerk only once the registration has been 
entered in WisVote. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)4.
Confidential Elector ID #
If the registrant has registered through the confidential elector process, they will 
be issued a number that should be listed here. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.33, 6.47(3).
Submitted by mail
If registrant mailed their voter registration application, check this circle.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
Official’s signature
The election official first receiving the application (election registration official, 
clerk, election inspector) should review the form for completeness and legibility 
before signing. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.32, 6.33(1).
If the application is incomplete or illegible, the election official should not sign 
the form. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2).
If the registrant is still available, ask the registrant to complete the missing 
information or print more clearly. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2).
Best Practice: If the registrant is no longer available, 
the election official should submit this form to the 
clerk with a note explaining the deficiency.
The clerk should contact the registrant within 5 days of receipt of any 
incomplete or illegible applications. Wis. Stat. § 6.32(2).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 20
Bottom Row
The clerk should record this information to properly determine the offices and  
referenda for which a voter is eligible to vote. This is entered when the registration  
is processed. In the case of Election Day registrations, it must be done right 
away to make sure the voter gets the correct ballot. Wis. Stat. § 6.33(1).
 Ɋ Ward
 Ɋ Sch. District
 Ɋ Alder
 Ɋ City Supr.
 Ɋ Ct. of App
 Ɋ Assembly
 Ɋ St. Senate
 Ɋ Congress
Back Side of Voter Registration Application
If the registrant resides somewhere without a designated address, the registrant 
should use the map in box 4 on the backside to diagram where they reside in 
relation to known streets or landmarks. Wis. Stat. § 6.10(1).
If the registrant needs accommodations at their polling place (curbside voting, 
braille materials, etc.), they should make those requests on the bottom of the 
application. Wis. Stat. § 6.36(1)(a)10.
If the registrant is interested in being a poll worker, they can indicate in the 
checkbox on the bottom of the application.
Sec. 6.2.4: Proof of Residence
Everyone (except military and permanent overseas electors and new and 
former Wisconsin residents) who wishes to register to vote or update their voter 
registration must present a proof of residence document to prove that the 
person resides at the address listed on the Voter Registration Application (EL-131). 
Wis. Stat. § 6.34. If the person is registering in-person with an election official, 
they do not need to provide a copy of the document for the election official to 
keep; they may simply show it to the election official so the official can verify the 
registration in real time. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.32, 6.34.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 21
Best Practice: Electronic versions of proof of residence are  
acceptable and can be displayed on a phone or other electronic  
device. The document must contain the voter’s current and  
complete name and current and complete Wisconsin residential  
address. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(b). If the document has an expiration  
date, it must not be expired on the day registration is made.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(c). Note that some documents (like a utility bill) 
do not have an expiration date and are still considered valid.
Note: Types of acceptable proof of residence are specifically listed by 
state law. Wis. Stat. § 6.34 . If a proof of residence document does not 
fall into one of the following categories, it cannot serve as acceptable 
proof of residence.
The following documents constitute acceptable proof of residence:
 Ɋ An unexpired Wisconsin Driver License or receipt for license, even if driving 
privileges were revoked or suspended. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)1.
 Ɋ An unexpired Wisconsin DOT–Issued Identification Card or receipt for 
identification card. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)2.
 Ɋ Any other official identification card or license issued by a Wisconsin 
governmental body or unit, unless otherwise prohibited by state law. Wis. 
Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)3. See Wis. Stat. § 66.0438 for special guidelines for locally-
issued identification documents.
 Ɋ Any identification card issued by an employer in the normal course of 
business and bearing a photo of the card holder, but not including a 
business card. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)4.
 Ɋ A real estate tax bill or receipt for the current year or the year preceding 
the date of the registration. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)5.
 Ɋ A utility bill for the period commencing not earlier than 90 days before 
Election Day. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)8.
 ɉ Examples include gas, electric, water, sewer, telephone/cell phone, 
cable/satellite, TV, Internet, etc.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 22
 Ɋ A residential lease. A residential lease should contain, at minimum:
 Ɉ Landlord Name
 Ɉ Tenant Name
 Ɉ Address Subject to Lease
 Ɉ Term
 Ɉ Rent
 Ɉ Landlord Signature
 Ɉ Tenant Signature
 ɉ If one or more of these are missing, it is up to the clerk to determine if 
the information contained is sufficient for proof of residence.
Note: A residential lease cannot be used as proof residence if a voter is 
registering by mail or online. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(2).
 Ɋ A university, college or technical institute identification card (must 
include photo, address not required) with one of the following:
 ɉ A fee payment receipt issued to the cardholder by the university, 
college, or technical college dated no earlier than 9 months before the 
date of the election. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)7.a.
 ɉ A certified and current list of students who reside in housing sponsored 
by the university, college, or technical college. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)7.b.
Note: This list should be provided by the university, college, or technical 
college and the election official must verify that the student presenting 
the card is included on the list.
 Ɋ Bank statement. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)9. This can include:
 Ɉ A bank statement issued by a bank or credit union
 Ɉ A mortgage statement issued by a bank or credit union
 Ɉ A home equity credit line statement issued by a bank or credit union
 Ɉ A credit card statement issued by a bank or credit union, but not an 
offer for a credit card
 Ɉ Paycheck or paystub documentation of direct deposit. Wis. Stat. 
§ 6.34(3)(a)10.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 23
 Ɋ A check or other document issued by a unit of government. Wis. Stat. 
§ 6.34(3)(a)10.
 ɉ Units of government include federal, state, county, municipal, school 
district, tribal, etc., both foreign and domestic.
 ɉ Examples of government documents (not an exhaustive list):
 Ɉ Vehicle registration
 Ɉ BadgerCare/Medicare statements3
 Ɉ Social Security statements3
 Ɉ Public school correspondence
 Ɉ Federal student loan notices3
 Ɉ Change of Address letter from the USPS.
 Ɉ Government-owned medical facilities, such as UW Hospitals and 
Clinics, county-owned health care clinics and VA Hospitals
 Ɉ A signed letter on public (government) social service agency 
letterhead identifying a homeless voter and describing the 
individual’s residence for voting purposes.
 Ɋ A contract or intake document from an occupant of a residential care 
facility, such as a nursing or group home, or community-based residential 
facility that specifies that the occupant currently resides in the facility. A 
room number is not required. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)12.
 Ɋ An identification card issued by a federally recognized Native American 
Wisconsin tribe. Wis. Stat. § 6.34(3)(a)(13).
3 If issued by a government agency
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 24
Electronic Proof of Residence
Otherwise valid proof of residence documents presented electronically on 
a device such as a laptop, smartphone, or tablet are acceptable for voter 
registration purposes.4 Electronic forms of proof of residence are not prohibited 
by state law. Wis. Stat. § 6.34, which requires only “an identifying document.”
The standard of review should be the same whether the document is 
physically presented to an election official or viewed in an electronic format.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.34 .
Election officials may not reject  an otherwise valid proof of residence 
merely because it is in an electronic format. See Id.  (requiring only “an 
identifying document”).
If the document is not readable in the format presented or the election official is 
otherwise unable to determine that it constitutes a valid proof of residence, the 
election official may reject the document and require the registrant to present 
another form of proof of residence. Id.
Election officials are not required to provide computers or Internet access for 
voters to use to obtain electronic copies of proof of residence to facilitate voter 
registration. It is the responsibility of the registrant to show or provide a copy of 
their proof of residence. Id.
Election officials are not required to handle a registrant’s electronic device but 
may do so with the registrant’s permission.
Best Practice: If the proof of residence is presented using the 
registrant’s electronic device, the election official may ask the 
registrant to expand the size of the type or image, or otherwise 
navigate the document or image so that the election official may view 
any required information (i.e., name of the registrant, address, account 
number, date, type of document, and issuing entity or institution).
4 On August 28, 2012, the G.A.B. voted unanimously to allow electronic versions of acceptable proof of 
residence during the voter registration process.

Chapter 6.3: Confidential 
Voters
Confidential voters require additional administrative steps during registration 
to ensure that their personally identifiable information remains confidential. 
Confidential voters will almost always apply for confidential status and then 
complete their voter registration with the clerk.
Sec. 6.3.1: Definition
Confidential voters are victims of domestic abuse, sexual assault, continued 
stalking, or those who meet other statutory considerations which make them 
eligible to vote while also being qualified to have their name and address 
confidential to the public. Wis. Stat. § 6.47.
Sec. 6.3.2: Eligibility
An individual is eligible for a confidential listing in the poll list if the person:
 Ɋ Has been granted a protective order that is in effect. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(1)
(am)1.
 Ɋ Is a victim of domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking where a person 
has been charged with or convicted of such an offense, and the victim 
reasonably continues to be threatened by that individual. Wis. Stat. § 
6.47(1)(am)2.
 Ɋ Resides in a shelter. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(1)(am)3.
 ɉ “Shelter” means a place where at least four unrelated individuals  
reside that provides residential shelter to individuals whose  
personal security is or may be threatened by family members  
or other persons with whom the individuals have had contact.  
Wis. Stat. § 6.47(1)(e).
 Ɋ Received services from a domestic abuse or sexual assault victim services 
provider within the last 24 months. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(1)(am)4.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 28
Note: The Commission regularly posts lists of eligible domestic abuse 
or sexual assault victim services providers on elections.wi.gov under 
Confidential Voters.
 Ɋ Is a participant in the Wisconsin Department of Justice’s Safe at Home 
Address Confidentiality Program.1 Wis. Stat. § 6.47(1)(am)5.
Sec. 6.3.3: Making the Request
An eligible person may request a confidential listing by submitting 
a written request or Request for Confidential Listing (EL-146) 
to their municipal clerk along with one of the following:
 Ɋ A copy of a protective order that is still in effect. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(2).
 Ɋ A completed Affidavit of Sheriff, Chief of Police, or District Attorney (EL-147),  
dated within 30 days of the date of the request. Id.
 Ɋ A statement signed by the operator or an authorized agent of the operator 
of a shelter that is dated within 30 days of the date of the request, which 
indicates that the operator operates the shelter and that the individual 
making the request resides in the shelter. Id.
 Ɋ A statement signed by an authorized representative of a domestic abuse 
victim service provider or a sexual assault victim service provider that is 
dated within 30 days of the request. Id.
 Ɋ Confirmation from the Department of Justice that the requester is a 
participant of the Safe at Home program. Id.
A physically disabled individual who appears personally at the clerk’s 
office, accompanied by another voter of this state, may designate that 
voter to make a request under this subsection on his or her behalf. Id. A 
confidential voter must still register to vote the same as any other voter. 
Wis. Stat. §§ 6.27 , 6.47(2).
1 wisdoj.gov/Pages/CrimeVictimServices/safe-at-home-address-confidentiality-program.aspx
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 29
If the individual provides the necessary documentation to obtain a confidential 
listing, the clerk issues an Identification Card of Protected Individual (EL-148) to 
the protected individual and notes the identification serial number on the voter 
registration form in the space provided. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(3). The ID serial number 
is the HINDI (DOA Code) number assigned to the municipality plus a sequential 
number e.g., “13251-01.” 
Note: The Identification Card of Protected Individual (EL-148) is not 
available on elections.wi.gov and can only be obtained by contacting 
the Wisconsin Elections Commission. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(3).
Sec. 6.3.4: Poll Book Procedure
The confidential portion of the poll list will appear at the end of the poll 
list as a separate section containing the name of each confidential voter 
and their confidential voter identification number. See Sec. 14.6.6: “EDR for 
Confidential Voters”  for how confidential voters request and cast their ballot 
at their polling place.
The confidential portion of the poll list is NOT open to public inspection.  
Wis. Stat. §§ 6.87(6m), 6.47(2).
The municipal clerk may, upon request, disclose the existence of the list, the 
number of voters whose names appear on the list, and the number of those 
voters who have voted at any point in the proceedings. Wis. Stat. § 7.41(4).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 30
Sec. 6.3.5: Recordkeeping
The confidential voter’s voter registration should be kept in a separate 
confidential file, ordered alphabetically by confidential voter name or 
alphabetically and sequentially by street name, street number, and voter name 
at each address. Wis. Stat. § 6.35(1), (1m).
Best Practice: For the sake of uniformity, voter registration 
records for non-confidential and confidential voters, though 
stored separately, should be ordered in the same manner.
Confidential listings expire when any of the 
following occur, whichever is earlier:
 Ɋ The day the protective order expires. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(4)(a).
 Ɋ When the confidential voter no longer resides in a shelter. Id.
 Ɋ When updated information is received from Wisconsin DOJ Safe at Home 
program, sheriff, chief of police, or district attorney that indicates the 
person is no longer qualified for a confidential listing. Id., (5)(a)1.
 Ɋ 24 months have passed since the creation/renewal of the confidential 
listing. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(4)(a).
 ɉ Exception: Participants in Wisconsin DOJ’s Safe at Home program can 
keep their confidential status longer than 24 months. Their CV status 
expires on the date their participation in Safe at Home expires, or the 
date that they cancel their enrollment or are disqualified. Wis. Stat. § 
6.47(4)(b). Participants can stay enrolled in Safe at Home for five years. 
Wis. Stat. § 165.68(3)(b)4.a.
When a confidential listing expires, the clerk shall change the registration of the 
confidential voter to inactive unless the confidential voter files a new request for 
a confidential listing or registers as a non-confidential voter. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(6).
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 31
Important: Inactive confidential voter registrations must be kept 
confidential until destroyed under Wis. Stat. §§ 7.23(1)(c), 6.47(6).
Note: An individual whose listing is canceled may file a new request 
and requalify for confidential status. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(5)(b).
If the municipal clerk has notice that a confidential listing is scheduled to expire  
(end of the 24-month period or end of five years for Wisconsin DOJ Safe at Home  
program), the clerk shall provide 30 days’ notice to the confidential voter of the 
scheduled expiration of the listing. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(7)(a). The notice letter can be 
downloaded or printed from WisVote. The clerk can go to the confidential voter 
record, click on the “Letters” tab and select “Confidential Voter 30 Day Expiration 
Notice Letter” from the list, download or print it to send to the voter.
If the advance notice is not provided, the clerk shall notify the confidential  
voter upon changing their voter registration to inactive. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(7)(b).  
The notification could be sent via notice letters, which can be printed or 
downloaded from the voter record in WisVote. The clerks can click on “Letters” 
tab and select “Deactivation of Confidential Voter Notice Letter.”
Clerks should also cancel a voter’s confidential 
listing if any of the following occur:
 Ɋ Upon receipt of a law enforcement affidavit explaining that the person 
who was charged or convicted for the qualifying offense that led to the 
protected status is no longer charged or the conviction was vacated. Wis. 
Stat. §§ 6.47(5)(a)1., 6.47(10).
 Ɋ The voter legally changes their name or changes their address without 
notifying the clerk. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(5)(a)2., 3.
 Ɋ The clerk finds out that the confidential voter provided false information in 
order to obtain the listing. Wis. Stat. § 6.47(5)(a)4.
First Edition, June 2026 Voter Qualifications & Registration 6 – 32


Part 7 
Absentee Voting
Deadlines for Requests; Types of Absentee Voters; Special Voting 
Deputies; Military and Overseas Voters (UOCAVA); In-Person Absentee 
Voting (IPAV); Absentee Ballot Return; Certificate Envelope Requirements; 
Correcting Certificate Envelopes; Ballot Spoiling; Managing and 
Transporting Absentee Ballots; “Central Count” Jurisdictions.
Any voter who is unable or unwilling to vote at their polling place on Election Day 
may request and return an absentee ballot. Special absentee voting procedures 
exist for certain voter types, including indefinitely confined voters, military and 
overseas voters, and those who vote with the assistance of Special Voting Deputies 
(SVDs). Voters can return their absentee ballots by mail, in person, or by drop box. 
Absentee ballots are enclosed in certificate envelopes, which is where the witness 
will enter their information (where required). Municipal clerks can work with voters 
to help them correct errors or insufficiencies in the certificate envelope. In certain 
circumstances, absentee voters can receive a replacement ballot if theirs is spoiled 
or damaged. Municipal clerks are responsible for managing and transporting bal-
lots either to their polling places or to a “central count” location. Some jurisdictions 
choose to count all of their absentee ballots at one location, instead of having each 
polling place do it. 
First Edition, June 2026 Absentee Voting 7 – 1
Chapter 7.1:  Deadlines
A qualified voter who is unable or unwilling to appear at the polling place on 
Election Day may vote by absentee ballot. Wis. Stat. § 6.85(1).
Sec. 7.1.1:  Introduction
The Legislature has described a policy concerning 
absentee voting, which states that:
The legislature finds that voting is a constitutional right, the vigorous exercise 
of which should be strongly encouraged. In contrast, voting by absentee 
ballot is a privilege exercised wholly outside the traditional safeguards of the 
polling place. The legislature finds that the privilege of voting by absentee 
ballot must be carefully regulated to prevent the potential for fraud or abuse, 
to prevent overzealous solicitation of absent electors who may prefer not to 
participate in an election, to prevent undue influence on an absent elector to 
vote for or against a candidate or to cast a particular vote in a referendum, or 
other similar abuses. Wis. Stat. § 6.84(1).1 The Legislature has also provided an 
interpretation that: Notwithstanding Wis. Stat. § 5.01(1), with respect to matters 
relating to the absentee ballot process, Wis. Stat. § 6.86, 6.87(3)–(7), 9.01(1)(b)2. 
and 4. shall be construed as mandatory. Ballots cast in contravention of the 
procedures specified in those provisions may not be counted. Ballots counted 
in contravention of the procedures specified in those provisions may not be 
included in the certified result of any election. Wis. Stat. § 6.84(2).
Sec. 7.1.2:   General Application 
Requirements
Registered electors2 wishing to vote absentee must submit an absentee ballot 
request in writing to the municipal clerk, or make their application in person 
during in-person absentee voting (IPAV). Wis. Stat. § 6.86(1)(a).
1 The Wisconsin Supreme Court has found that this section “is merely a declaration of legislative 
policy setting forth that ‘absentee balloting must be carefully regulated.’ The subsequent statutes do 
just that. See Wis. Stat. §§ 6.84–6.89. Again, nothing in subsec. (1) provides any rule of interpretation 
applying to the statutes that follow.” Priorities USA v. Wis. Elections Comm’n, 2024 WI 32, ¶32, 412 Wis. 2d 
594, 8 N.W.3d 429.
2 With exceptions for new residents, former residents, and military electors who are not required to 
register prior to voting. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.15, 6.18, 6.22.
First Edition, June 2026 Absentee Voting 7 – 2
This section describes the general process of requesting an absentee ballot. 
However, there are many specific types of absentee voting, which are described 
in detail later in this chapter.
 Making a Written Request
The written request for an absentee ballot can appear on the Commission’s 
prescribed Application for Absentee Ballot (EL-121) form or within a letter, email, 
or fax written by the voter. As long as the request includes all the information 
necessary to provide the voter with an absentee ballot, it must be processed 
and an absentee ballot sent. Wis. Stat. § 6.86.
Exception: For indefinitely confined, calendar year, and hospitalized voter 
absentee ballot requests, the voter must use the Form EL-121, due to a statutory 
quirk that requires the use of the actual form. If a clerk receives an absentee 
ballot request from one of these voter types that is not on the EL-121, the clerk 
should contact the voter and direct them to resubmit the request on the EL-121 
form. Wis. Stat. § 6.86(2), (2m), (3) (each requiring the use of an application form 
“prescribed by the Commission”).
Note for Email Requests Submitted through MyVote: Clerks are still fully 
responsible for determining if an absentee ballot request submitted through the 
Commission’s MyVote website is sufficient. MyVote enables voters to make the 
request, but does not guarantee that it is fully sufficient, nor does it guarantee 
that the voter has submitted acceptable photo ID if required. Additionally, 
clerks must take action to issue the absentee ballot — MyVote won’t do it 
automatically. Clerks are responsible for contacting the voter if there are any 
insufficiencies with absentee requests submitted through MyVote. See Chapter 
3.5 of the WisVote Manual for instructions on reviewing and issuing absentee 
ballots from MyVote requests.
First Edition, June 2026 Absentee Voting 7 – 3
 Components of a Sufficient Written Request
The written request must include the voter’s:
 Ɋ Name. Wis. Stat. § 6.86(1)(ar).
 Ɋ Residential address. Wis. Stat. § 6.87(3)(a).
 Ɋ Mailing address, if different than residential address. Wis. Stat. § 6.87(3)(a).
 Ɋ Signature (unless requested via email or fax). Wis. Stat. § 6.86(1)(ac). A 
voter who is unable to write the voter’s name due to a disability may 
authorize another individual to make an absentee ballot application. 
The request must state that assistance has been provided at the voter’s 
“request and by authorization of a named elector who is unable to sign 
the application due to physical disability.” Wis. Stat. § 6.86(1)(ag). On the EL-
121, there is an assistant declaration section for the assistant to sign.
 Ɋ Proof of identification (shown and verified if in person; provided as a 
copy if by mail, email, or fax, but not required for military, overseas voter, 
indefinitely confined, SVD, or confidential voters or for voters who have 
provided proof of ID for a prior absentee ballot under the voter’s current 
name and address). Wis. Stat. §§ 6.86(1)(ac) and 6.87(1).
 Submitting the Written Request
Any absentee ballot request, which may be a scan of a paper form, can be 
submitted by an voter via fax or email and the process for handling the request 
is exactly the same except that such a request does not need to contain the 
signature of the voter to be valid. Wis. Stat. § 6.86(1)(ac).3
Any registered voter may also submit an absentee ballot request by mail. Wis. 
Stat. § 6.86(1)(a)1. However, a voter can only deliver an absentee ballot request 
in person to a municipal clerk during the in-person absentee voting period. Wis. 
Stat. § 6.86(1)(a)2., (ar) and (b).
3 The elector requesting via fax or email is required to provide a copy of the request with the voter’s 
original signature when the ballot is returned, and the Commission has designed the certificate 
envelope to function as a copy of the request, with the signature of the certificate therefore fulfilling 
this requirement. Wis. Stat. § 6.86(1)(ac) and see Thomas Oldenburg v. WEC et al., (Marinette County 
Circuit Court, Branch 2, 2024CV000043; July 29, 2024 Oral Ruling). Additionally, the certificate envelope 
also functions as an absentee ballot request by mail, which does not require a copy of the request to 
be provided because the certificate envelope already contains the voter’s signature.
First Edition, June 2026 Absentee Voting 7 – 4
Best practice: If someone attempts to deliver an absentee ballot 
request outside of the in-person absentee voting period, the clerk 
should explain that it cannot be accepted, but that the request can be 
mailed to the clerk, or an application can be completed on MyVote.
Sec. 7.1.3:  A Voter’s Agent Possessing 
the Voter’s Power of Attorney (POA) 
May Not Cast Voter’s Ballot
A voter’s agent under a POA may NOT vote the ballot for the voter because 
only an voter is able to make the voter’s own voting choices. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.80 
(polling place) 6.87(2) and 6.87(4)(b)1. (absentee), and see Wis. Stat § 12.13(1)(d) 
(prohibiting impersonating an voter). An agent operating under a voter’s POA 
may serve as an assistant in all the same ways that any person may serve 
as an assistant. Wis. Stat. §§ 6.82 (assistance in voting the polls), 6.86(1)(ag) 
(assisting in signing an absentee request), and 6.87(5) (assistance in voting an 
absentee ballot).
